correctness.rationale: The exact domain is sixteen binary edge coordinates and all 4096 seven-edge spanning trees of \(K_{4,4}\). Two independent implementations agree pointwise on all 65536 character multipliers: (1) 192 row/column/transpose orbits with exact signed-Laplacian cofactors by fraction-free integer elimination and (2) exact union-find enumeration of all seven-edge trees followed by a 16-stage integer Walsh-Hadamard transform. Both yield 42894 zeros, 22642 nonzero values and minimal nonzero magnitude 32; Parseval and complement-sign symmetry are checked. A further exact transform of the Fourier range indicator gives kernel absolute sum 2950060, hence sharp endpoint norm 2950060/65536=737515/16384. This proves a complete finite statement without extrapolation.

value.rationale: The balanced four-by-four complete bipartite graph is a canonical first sizeable square case with sixteen edge-sign coordinates, and the complete Fourier spectrum measures exact identifiability of parity observations of its uniform spanning-tree codebook. The 22642-versus-42894 recoverability boundary, minimal positive multiplier 32, and sharp endpoint range-projection norm 737515/16384 are precise natural Fourier invariants not implied numerically by the generic counting formula. The 192-orbit integral certificate and pointwise-independent replay make this a complete and reproducible finite benchmark, not an arbitrary parameter slice or small delta in an already tabulated sequence.
